journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Sustainability skills in vocational education: limited integration of financial and economic competencies
text_snippet: Sustainability skills in vocational education: limited integration of financial and economic competencies Abstract This paper examines how sustainability competencies are conceptualized within vocational education and training (VET) and their implications for career development. It combines a bibliometric review of 604 publications (1990–2026) with a scoping review of 118 studies. The findings reveal a consistent imbalance: sustainability is predominantly framed through environmental competencies, while financial and economic dimensions remain weakly integrated. This limits the development of broader competency profiles relevant to emerging occupational pathways. The paper identifies this persistent gap and discusses implications for vocational guidance in supporting sustainable career transitions.

title: How do leaders’ expressions of gratitude relate to subordinates’ promotion focus? Links to job crafting and voice
text_snippet: How do leaders’ expressions of gratitude relate to subordinates’ promotion focus? Links to job crafting and voice Abstract We explore the impact of leader gratitude expression on subordinates’ proactive career behaviors, job crafting (seeking resources, seeking challenges, and reducing demands) and voice behaviors (promotive and prohibitive voice), and the mediating mechanism by subordinate promotion focus. A survey data from 597 full-time employees, analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapping analyses, supported hypothesized relationships. Promotion focus mediated the relationship between leader gratitude expression and all dimensions of job crafting and voice behaviors. This study contributes to the literature on leadership and regulatory focus. We discuss future research and implications for leadership practice and career self-management.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Systemically narrating career adaptability: exploring the application of the My System of Career Influences with migrant university students
text_snippet: Systemically narrating career adaptability: exploring the application of the My System of Career Influences with migrant university students Abstract Migrant university students navigate career transitions shaped by diverse systemic influences. Career adaptability is key to navigating the twenty-first-century labor market, yet little is known about the practical link between qualitative career assessment instruments and career adaptability. This study explores the My System of Career Influences (MSCI) for systemically narrating career adaptability. Data from 7 migrant students across 14 semi-structured interviews were analyzed using a theory-driven deductive thematic analysis. Findings highlight the MSCI’s role in helping students reflect on their systemic career influences and reconstructing career adaptability narratives. Implications for career research, practice, and future directions are discussed.

title: Integrating career guidance and counseling into the high school curriculum in Lesotho: challenges and best practices
text_snippet: Integrating career guidance and counseling into the high school curriculum in Lesotho: challenges and best practices Abstract This study explores the integration of career guidance and counseling into Lesotho’s high school curriculum, focusing on challenges and best practices. Using qualitative secondary analysis of interviews and focus group transcripts from 123 participants across 10 schools, the research was guided by Krumboltz’s Social Learning Theory of Career Decision Making. Thematic analysis revealed five interrelated themes: resource limitations, teacher training gaps, curriculum rigidity, informal influences, and emerging best practices. Findings underscore the urgent need for systemic support, professional counselors, and curriculum reform to embed career guidance as a core component of secondary education, enhancing equity and student preparedness.

title: Challenges in women’s work trajectories: a systematic review of the contributions of career construction theory
text_snippet: Challenges in women’s work trajectories: a systematic review of the contributions of career construction theory Abstract Transformations in the world of work have made traditional career models insufficient, requiring more comprehensive approaches. For women, this reality adds to persistent gender inequalities. This systematic review examined how Career Construction Theory (CCT) has been used to understand women’s career trajectories. Seventeen studies, primarily qualitative and conducted in the Global South, employed CCT as a theoretical lens, narrative intervention, or via Career Adaptability. The findings highlight structural and economic barriers, indicating that CCT can be a powerful resource for promoting self-awareness and meaningful career construction in contexts of vulnerability.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: The fetishisation of digital platforms for graduate career development
text_snippet: The fetishisation of digital platforms for graduate career development Abstract This article theorises digital platforms for career development as an example of technological fetishisation. Through a longitudinal study of 22 UK graduates interviewed across their transition from university, six narrative typologies emerged describing graduates’ platform relationships. Findings reveal graduates maintained strong beliefs in platforms’ transformative power despite limited tangible benefits, while remaining uncritical of business models and overlooking harassment, precarity and surveillance. Theorised as fetishisation through ‘irrational beliefs’ and ‘veiled realities’, this challenges instrumental ‘digital career literacy’ accounts that position platforms as inherently progressive, instead offering a critical perspective on the relationship between career development and digital technology.

title: Adaptation of the decent work for inclusive and sustainable future construction scale in Türkiye
text_snippet: Adaptation of the decent work for inclusive and sustainable future construction scale in Türkiye Abstract The world of work needs a concept of decent work that promotes a future characterized by inclusiveness, respect for human rights, and sustainability for everyone. This study aims to adapt the Decent Work for Inclusive and Sustainable Future Construction Scale (DW-ISFCS) into Turkish, a scale that addresses this need. A sample of 354 Turkish university students completed the adapted scale, the Future Decent Work Scale, the Career Adapt-Abilities Scale–sSort Form, and the Satisfaction with Life Scale. Confirmatory factor analysis, measurement invariance analysis, item response analysis, reliability assessments, and criterion-related validity analyses were conducted. The confirmatory factor analysis results confirmed the six-item unidimensional structure of the scale. Invariance analysis demonstrated that the scale provided configural, metric, and scalar invariance across gender groups. Item response analysis indicated that the items had sufficient discriminatory power. The reliability of the DW-ISFCS was confirmed through multiple analyses. Finally, the scale showed positive correlations with future decent work perceptions and career adaptability, but no significant relation

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: The comparative role of individual differences and marginalization factors in predicting NEET status
text_snippet: The comparative role of individual differences and marginalization factors in predicting NEET status Abstract Both individual and social factors contribute to the risk of becoming not in education, employment, or training (NEET) and to lower self-perceived employability, yet few studies have examined their relative importance. We compared 197 NEETs aged 16–25 years enrolled in a vocational support program and 205 peers in education or employment. Measures included personality traits, adaptive resources, and marginalization factors (e.g., nationality, school background). Results indicate that marginalization factors were more strongly associated with NEET status, whereas personality traits were more strongly associated with perceived employability—highlighting the relevance of integrated, personalized approaches in vocational guidance, and related public policies.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Consciously uncertain but knowing in action: exploring how the concept of career competence resonates with guidance counsellors
text_snippet: Consciously uncertain but knowing in action: exploring how the concept of career competence resonates with guidance counsellors Abstract This qualitative study uses career competence and career management skills interchangeably to explore how the concept resonates with guidance counsellors in practice. It is inspired by sayings and doings in practice theory and draws on the two theoretical concepts of sensemaking and professional artistry. Semi-structured interviews were analysed using reflective thematic analysis. The findings reveal that while guidance counsellors said career competence is a challenging and de-prioritised concept, actions were in line with the learning goals for career competence in the core curriculum. This contrast between sayings and doings indicate that professional artistry may compensate for a nascent sensemaking process of the concept. The study points to the importance of treating the concept of career competence as a field of knowledge in both steering documents and the guidance counselling profession to create stronger resonance.

title: The mediating role of academic self-efficacy and moderating role of age in the relationship between career optimism and academic outcome expectations
text_snippet: The mediating role of academic self-efficacy and moderating role of age in the relationship between career optimism and academic outcome expectations Abstract The present study examined the relationship between career optimism and academic outcome expectations, the mediating role of academic self-efficacy, and the moderating role of age in this relationship. The study participants consisted of 287 university students from Türkiye. The structural equation modeling results demonstrated that career optimism and academic outcome expectations were positively related, and academic self-efficacy mediated this relationship. Results also showed that age moderated the relationship between career optimism and academic outcome expectations, with the relationship between career optimism and academic outcome expectations not being significant for relatively older college students. Implications for theory and practice are discussed.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Examining factors influencing adolescents’ career aspirations using systems theory framework: the case of Qatar
text_snippet: Examining factors influencing adolescents’ career aspirations using systems theory framework: the case of Qatar Abstract This study examined factors influencing the career aspirations of 1640 high school students in Qatari schools. Guided by the systems theory framework, a survey including factors within the intrapersonal, social, and environmental–societal systems of influence was devised. Results indicated the complex, dynamic, and interrelated nature of the factors influencing career aspirations, with some demographic characteristics playing a more prominent role than others. Regarding the systems of influence, the factors with the highest average percentages were those pertaining to the environmental–societal system, while intrapersonal factors were not significant influencers on career aspirations. These results have implications for career development professionals and schools.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Future working prospects of urban emerging adults in post-pandemic Brazil
text_snippet: Future working prospects of urban emerging adults in post-pandemic Brazil Abstract The pandemic highly impacted the working world and career construction, and emerging adults are one of the most affected groups. Through in-depth interviews, the study aimed to identify, understand and contrast the future working prospects in the post-pandemic among 20 low- and high-skilled emerging adults in Brazil, using consensual qualitative research. Findings indicated both demanded stability, the need to study to improve job skills and greater solidarity. However, while low-skilled participants expressed hopelessness and the need to improve the quality of work, high-skilled ones sought to be promoted within their current job, looked for new opportunities or intended to be entrepreneurs.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Artificial intelligence applications supporting women’s career development: a scoping review
text_snippet: Artificial intelligence applications supporting women’s career development: a scoping review Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into career guidance and organisational decision systems, yet empirical evidence on applications designed to support women’s career development remains limited. Following the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR) and a preregistered protocol, we searched seven databases (plus backward and forward citation searching) and synthesised 13 empirical studies published between 2018 and 2025. Using inductive thematic analysis, we identified three functional domains: (1) bias mitigation and representation (e.g. auditing gendered language and platform-level disparities), (2) skills development and empowerment (e.g. AI-supported learning and writing interventions) and (3) career pathways and retention (e.g. matching and attrition-risk modelling). The evidence base was concentrated in system-facing applications that detect or shape inequities within recruitment, evaluation and exposure systems; fewer studies evaluated individual-facing developmental support, and sustained career outcomes were rarely measured. title: Exploring the link between family support and career adaptability: a meta-analytic perspective
text_snippet: Exploring the link between family support and career adaptability: a meta-analytic perspective Abstract Social support plays a vital role in shaping individuals’ career aspirations and building confidence to overcome academic and professional challenges. Within social support, family support and parental role modeling are particularly influential in guiding career development. This meta-analysis examined the association between family support and career adaptability. A systematic search of Web of Science, Scopus, and ProQuest yielded 26 quantitative studies comprising 28 independent samples ( N = 35,821). Using Comprehensive Meta-Analysis software, results indicated a positive and statistically significant association, moderated by cultural orientation, developmental stage, and the measurement of career adaptability. Overall, the findings suggest that while the relationship remains positive, its magnitude varies across developmental, cultural, and measurement contexts.

title: Racial microaggressions and decent work among Black Brazilian workers: a partial test of the psychology of working theory
text_snippet: Racial microaggressions and decent work among Black Brazilian workers: a partial test of the psychology of working theory Abstract The Psychology of Working Theory (PWT) is a social-justice-oriented framework that examines how structural conditions shape access to decent work, particularly among marginalized populations. This study advances the PWT by examining racial microaggressions as psychosocial mechanisms of marginalization in a Global South context. Specifically, we tested a partial PWT model to analyze how exposure to racial microaggressions and work volition relate to perceptions of decent work among Black Brazilian workers. Using a survey design with 335 working adults, the results showed that multiple dimensions of racial microaggressions mediated the relationship between economic constraints and decent work. Work volition also played a significant mediating role, functioning as a psychological resource in contexts marked by racial and socioeconomic inequities. Overall, the findings extend the applicability of the PWT by enhancing its sensitivity to contemporary forms of racial exclusion in the workplace. journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Perspectives of the future, identity, and career constructions among college students in the face of the climate crisis: an outlook from Southern countries
text_snippet: Perspectives of the future, identity, and career constructions among college students in the face of the climate crisis: an outlook from Southern countries Abstract This study aimed to identify, understand, and compare the career constructions and future working prospects of college students in Southern countries amid the climate crisis. Researchers conducted in-depth interviews with 50 participants—10 from each of the following countries: Brazil, Burkina Faso, Iran, Lebanon, and Tunisia, and used content analysis. Findings show that, despite differences, Southern countries face similar struggles. Conflicting emotions regarding climate change shape students’ future careers and life outlooks, sparking activism or specific actions. The climate crisis impacts life, education, and career planning. The study concludes that career guidance and counseling should address climate issues more directly.

title: Assessing the effects of career construction counseling on career adaptability for graduate students of business administration
text_snippet: Assessing the effects of career construction counseling on career adaptability for graduate students of business administration Abstract This quantitative, explanatory, and quasi-experimental study evaluated the effects of Career Construction Counseling on the career adaptability of graduate students in Business Administration at a state university in Santa Catarina, Brazil. A total of 41 students participated, divided into an intervention group and a control group. The data were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Pearson’s correlation. The results revealed significant changes in the four dimensions of career adaptability, which remained 3 months after the intervention, as well as significant correlations between adaptability and sociodemographic variables such as age, marital status, education level, and presence of children. Implications for future research and practice are discussed.

title: Linking career exploration and decision self-efficacy to career engagement: a sequential mediation model of career adaptability and career calling
text_snippet: Linking career exploration and decision self-efficacy to career engagement: a sequential mediation model of career adaptability and career calling Abstract In the current dynamic employment environment, individuals require personal resources to navigate unforeseen career challenges. This study investigates the relationship between career exploration and decision self-efficacy and career engagement, with career adaptability and career calling serving as sequential mediators. Data were gathered from 211 university students in Turkey employing a time-lagged approach. Structural equation modeling demonstrated that the relationship between career exploration and decision self-efficacy positively impacts career engagement and was sequentially mediated by career adaptability and career calling. The findings provide practical implications for higher education institutions and career counseling practices.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Care as the sine qua non: a proposal for situating an ethic of care within the social justice agenda of career development research and practice
text_snippet: Care as the sine qua non: a proposal for situating an ethic of care within the social justice agenda of career development research and practice Abstract This article proposes an ‘integrative ethical lens’ that positions care ethics as a bridge between social justice values and goals, addressing a key ethical gap to facilitate context-responsive research and practice actions. It critiques limitations of approaches underpinned solely by justice-ethics traditions, and building on the narrative turn, offers a pragmatic, action-focused framework grounded in the foundational elements of care. Foregrounding epistemic justice, the lens clarifies how social justice can be enacted through attuned career research and practice that are reimagined as ethical projects, where responsively attending to diverse voices and local knowledges is foundational to meaningful social justice.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Academic engagement, academic self-efficacy and instructor support in higher education: impacts on postgraduate career intention
text_snippet: Academic engagement, academic self-efficacy and instructor support in higher education: impacts on postgraduate career intention Abstract Although postgraduate education has received increasing attention, little research has examined the cognitive and contextual factors shaping undergraduates’ intentions to pursue a postgraduate career. Guided by social cognitive career theory, this study examined the mediating role of academic engagement in the relationship between academic self-efficacy and postgraduate career intention and the moderating role of perceived instructor support. Participants were 302 undergraduate students from a university in Türkiye. Findings showed that academic self-efficacy had a direct effect on postgraduate career intention. Academic engagement significantly mediated this relationship. Moderated mediation analyses revealed that perceived instructor support strengthened both the direct and indirect effects, with the indirect path through academic engagement being more pronounced at higher levels of instructor support.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Exploring the relationship between career exploration behaviors and social cognitive factors among middle school students
text_snippet: Exploring the relationship between career exploration behaviors and social cognitive factors among middle school students Abstract The primary objective of this study was to investigate the correlations among self-efficacy, outcome expectations, goal commitment, parental support, and career exploration behaviors among middle school students. To this end, the study sampled 452 middle school students from a medium-sized city in the Black Sea region of Türkiye. Data analysis was conducted using Pearson’s correlation, regression analysis, t -tests, and one-way ANOVA. The results indicated significant negative correlations among career decision-making self-efficacy, career outcome expectations, goal commitment, parental support, and career exploration. In other words, it was determined that, as middle school students’ confidence levels regarding career decisions, positive outcome expectations, commitment to career goals, and perceptions of parental support increased, their career exploration behaviors decreased significantly. Additionally, all variables except outcome expectations significantly predicted career exploration.

title: The mediating role of learned meaninglessness in the relationship between Hikikomori and unemployment anxiety among Turkish university students
text_snippet: The mediating role of learned meaninglessness in the relationship between Hikikomori and unemployment anxiety among Turkish university students Abstract This study examines the relationship between unemployment anxiety, learned meaninglessness, and hikikomori tendencies among university students in Türkiye, emphasizing the mediating role of learned meaninglessness. Analysis of 445 students shows that unemployment anxiety predicts hikikomori tendencies, amplified by learned meaninglessness. Students from lower-income backgrounds and those living alone exhibit higher hikikomori tendencies, while gender, age, and academic year have no significant impact. The study highlights that unemployment anxiety predicts hikikomori tendencies, and that this relationship is partially mediated by learned meaninglessness. Supporting individuals’ sense of purpose and reducing unemployment-related concerns may help mitigate hikikomori risk.

title: Can i still dream of a decent work? the interplay of economic constraints, perceived employability, and social support
text_snippet: Can i still dream of a decent work? the interplay of economic constraints, perceived employability, and social support Abstract Guided by the school-to-work transition (STWT) model, this study examined how economic constraints affect university students’ perceptions of future decent work, with perceived employability as a mediator and social support as a moderator. Using a cross-sectional survey of 652 students, results showed that economic constraints negatively predicted both employability and decent work perceptions. Employability partially mediated this relationship, while social support moderated the effect of economic constraints on employability. These findings underscore the importance of contextual and psychosocial factors in shaping students’ vocational outlooks and offer insights for career counseling practices targeting economically disadvantaged youth.

title: A qualitative examination of career adaptation of LGBT+ individuals
text_snippet: A qualitative examination of career adaptation of LGBT+ individuals Abstract This study explores LGBT+ (Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and other sexual and gender minority identities) individuals’ career adaptation processes through the career construction model of career construction theory. Employing a qualitative, phenomenological design, data were collected from 15 participants via snowball sampling using a personal information form and semistructured interviews. Content analysis revealed 14 themes and 31 categories across four dimensions: adaptivity, adaptability (concern, control, curiosity, confidence), adapting responses, and adaptation results. Participants reported challenges in career decision-making and exploration. Some preferred working in socially accepting countries. Coming out influenced the effectiveness of coping strategies in job search and the workplace.

title: STEM career interests of Ghanaian adolescents in the context of social cognitive career theory
text_snippet: STEM career interests of Ghanaian adolescents in the context of social cognitive career theory Abstract This study sought to determine whether the social cognitive career theory (SCCT), which posits that interest is shaped by self-efficacy and outcome expectancies as well as experiences with sources of influence and prior learning, reflects factors likely to influence Ghanaian adolescents’ interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) careers ( N = 209, mean age = 17.03 years). Findings indicate that social influences such as the presence role models and interactions with family, teachers, and peers were highly influential. Moreover, unlike Western settings, self-efficacy did not predict career interest for Ghanaians. Finally, different factors were associated with different STEM careers, suggesting the need to examine distinct careers separately.

journal_name: International Journal for Educational and Vocational Guidance
title: Information approaches and the construction of ‘good’ guidance in career guidance counsellors’ professional practice
text_snippet: Information approaches and the construction of ‘good’ guidance in career guidance counsellors’ professional practice Abstract Adopting a reflexive research approach, this study offers insights into how career guidance counsellors (CGCs) conceptualise the role of information in their work with students, and how its use aligns with their notions of good practice. In total, 25 CGCs were interviewed to describe and reflect on how they support upper secondary students’ transition to continuing education and work. The iterative engagement between theory and data enabled the identification of five different approaches to information use in guidance practice. The five approaches embody a spectrum of theoretical orientations, ranging from traditional matching paradigms to emancipatory perspectives. The analysis highlights an information paradox, concluding that information may have multiple roles in guidance. Although matching-oriented perspectives on information are prominent in their everyday practices, this study suggests that information use grounded in developmental and socially informed theoretical frameworks aligns more closely with CGCs’ conceptions of good guidance.

title: The conceptions of decent work and characteristics that influence it among Swiss students in vocational and professional education and training
text_snippet: The conceptions of decent work and characteristics that influence it among Swiss students in vocational and professional education and training Abstract This study examined how 770 Swiss students in vocational and professional education and training define decent work, addressing a gap in literature. Through questionnaires, researchers collected definitions along with demographic, psychological, and education/work-related data. Deductive qualitative analysis identified 14 key aspects, including fair pay, physical and psychological safety, and sufficient rest and leisure—aligning with the Psychology of Working Theory. Positive workplace relationships were frequently emphasized, while respect for workers emerged as a cross-cutting theme. Definitions varied by gender and educational track. The findings enrich theoretical understanding of decent work and provide valuable insights for educators, counselors, employers, and policymakers.

title: Cultural translation of career decision-making: understanding practitioners’ perspectives from a multinational study on social and emotional learning
text_snippet: Cultural translation of career decision-making: understanding practitioners’ perspectives from a multinational study on social and emotional learning Abstract The purpose of this study was to examine the practices and philosophies of educators in nine countries, regarding career decision-making. We surveyed educators’ perceptions, created codebooks, and conducted cluster analysis using the data related to career decision-making. As a result, we found patterns within the differences: career decision-making as part of survival skills (South Africa and Burkina Faso), the negotiation of decision-making holders (Greece and Türkiye), influencing problems of adults in children’s decision-making (Italy, Poland, Japan, and Romania), and involving management skills (Türkiye and USA). We discuss the different ways to understand career decision-making and multinational study.

title: Revisiting factors influencing career development of international students
text_snippet: Revisiting factors influencing career development of international students Abstract The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic significantly impacted international students’ career development. Using Social Cognitive Career Theory, this study explored how learning experiences influenced career decision self-efficacy (CDSE) and career outcome expectations (COE). Data from 354 international students (70.1% master’s; 83.9% Asian) at a US university in 2021–2022 were analyzed via structural equation modeling. Results showed learning experiences positively predicted CDSE and COE, with CDSE mediating their relationship. Career counselors can enhance support by fostering confidence-building interventions. These findings highlight confidence as key to international students’ career development, especially amid systemic challenges. Implications for practice and future research are provided.
